paragraphs: A) In the Mishnah: Berakhot 1:3; 6:5; chapter 8 (see Beit Shammai; they are mentioned together everywhere). Sheviit 10:3; 11:2 [as printed; Sheviit has no chapter 11]; Gittin 4:3; Bava Metzia 5:9; Eduyot 1:1, 2, 3; Arakhin 9:4; Niddah 1:1.

B) Patriarch of Israel, descended on his father’s side from Benjamin and on his mother’s side from Shefatyah, David’s fifth son, as it says, “The fifth, Shefatyah, son of Avital,” David’s wife: Bereshit Rabbah chapters 33 and 98; Ketubbot, chapter Hanose (see above, Rabbi Chiyya); chapter Bammeh Behemah, “Rabbi, who comes from David …,” see there; Tosafot, Sanhedrin chapter 1, 5a: the Babylonian exilarch descends through the males and the patriarch in the Land of Israel through the females of David’s seed (see above, Rav Huna the exilarch). Under Nechemyah, in the order of the generations, Yuchasin writes that in Sanhedrin, chapter Dinei Mamonot, Zerubbabel is Nechemyah ben Chakhalyah, and they say Hillel descended from him; but from the Talmud it appears he descended from Shefatyah. (Shalshelet HaKabbalah 26a writes: some say Hillel was the brother of Chizkiyah mentioned in the chain of David’s descendants, who remained in Babylonia over the patriarchate; see Semag, positive commandments 148 and 223. I found nothing of this. Sefer Berit Menuchah, 2, beginning of side b, writes that this Hillel was among the descendants of Nearyah of David’s descendants, found in Chronicles.) He is the head of the patriarchal family. The law that the Passover offering at its appointed time overrides the Sabbath was hidden from the sons of Beteira; Hillel knew it, and they appointed Hillel patriarch. Why was the law hidden from them? To give greatness to Hillel, as stated at the beginning of chapter Ellu Devarim, Pesachim 66a.

C) His patriarchate began one hundred years before the destruction. Hillel and Shammai were students of Shemayah and Avtalyon (Avot chapter 1); they received in year 3728 from creation, 320 from the Temple’s construction. In Nazir chapter 3, 19, end of side b, and Ketubbot 7a, Beit Hillel instructed Queen Hilleni to be a nazirite another seven years. Tosafot writes there, side b: “Although Hilleni was of the Hasmonean house, being King Monobaz’s mother, as stated in Yoma 37, and Herod’s reign was 103 years while the Temple stood, Hillel did not exercise the patriarchate until three years after the start of Herod’s reign, as Shabbat 15a says: Hillel, Shimon, Gamliel and Shimon exercised the patriarchate for 100 years while the Temple stood. Nevertheless he already had students then who instructed her.” End of quotation. This requires examination: three years after Herod is 3764; thus Hillel’s patriarchate extended from 3728 to 3764, 36 years, whereas the sages said he led for forty years. He lived 120 years: at forty he went up from Babylonia, forty years he studied, and forty he led Israel. Sefer Keritot, Yemot Olam, section 15, writes that Hillel and Shammai were members of the Sanhedrin in the Second Temple.

D) Initially there were Hillel and Menachem (see his entry). In Menachem’s days Shammai was Hillel’s student; afterwards Shammai was Hillel’s student-colleague. He was very humble, as stated in Shabbat, chapter Bammeh Madlikin, 30. From his great humility he altered the truth for peace: the burnt offering was male, but he said it was female for a peace offering, Beitzah 20, end of side a. He therefore merited that the law be established like him, as stated in Eruvin chapter 1, 13b: because they were gentle and forbearing, taught their own words and Beit Shammai’s, and placed Beit Shammai’s words before their own (see Shammai, what is written there about why they placed Beit Shammai first). Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot chapter 1: a heavenly voice came forth that the law follows Beit Hillel. See Jerusalem Talmud, Yevamot chapter 1: Rabbi Bibi in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, in Yavneh a heavenly voice declared the law follows Beit Hillel. See Mabit’s responsa, part 2,section 20. Except for one law in Terumot chapter 5, where Beit Shammai retracted to rule like Beit Hillel, Beit Shammai did not otherwise retract to rule like Beit Hillel. (On 9 Adar, Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagreed.) They disagreed in only three matters, as stated in Shabbat chapter 1, 14b; the disputes between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel arose among their successors, who had not attended them sufficiently: Sotah 47; Sanhedrin 88. “Beit Shammai in the place of Beit Hillel is not a mishnah.” Some explain this to mean that if Beit Shammai are lenient and Beit Hillel stringent, and they are not among the anonymous mishnayot mentioned in Eduyot, it is not a mishnah: one must treat the mishnah as corrupt and reverse the reading. See Tosafot Yom Tov, Kol HaBasar, mishnah 1; Niddah 4:3; beginning of Niddah; beginning of Yevamot chapter 3. Nevertheless, in most Talmudic occurrences of this expression it cannot be explained thus; see Berakhot 36b; Beitzah chapter 1, 11b; Yevamot chapter 1, 9a; Rashi, Shabbat 135a; Tosafot, Eruvin 72b and Chagigah 6a; Rif, beginning of Hazahav; chapter Mi Shemet. Most prove that “not a mishnah” means Beit Shammai’s words are entirely null, as though never mentioned, and rank below other Tannaitic disputes. It seems to me the reason is that Beit Hillel are the majority, together with the heavenly voice’s assent, as Tosafot writes concerning Akhnai’s oven. (See above, Shammai: in six places the law follows Beit Shammai; Chavvot Yair’s responsum; and Sefer Melo Ratzon at its end.) Hillel, Rabbi Eliezer the Great, our holy master, and the Ari, of blessed memory, are the secret of Yesod of Abba, or of Zeir Anpin, or of Yaakov (Ch.S.L.,spring 5,river 25). Hillel is from the side of kindness (see Shammai); see R.M.,Pinchas. Hillel and Shammai: one is from Abel’s merciful side and one from Abel’s judgment, kindness and fear, the levels of Abraham and Isaac. See G.N.,letter dalet: Hillel is David. They expounded, “The Lord was with him,” meaning the law follows him; likewise the law follows Hillel. Shammai is Yonatan: as the sages say in Chelek, in every matter Saul said, “My son is like him,” but when told that the law follows him, his spirit weakened. Likewise the law does not follow Beit Shammai. Under letter vav it writes: Hillel is Solomon’s reincarnation; “I turned to see wisdom and folly”—holelot hints at Hillel. His root was Yesod, which is mercy, so he did not become angry. Shammai was Yehoshua ben Nun’s reincarnation; this is “what he has already done.” His root was Malkhut, which is might and judgment; therefore Shammai was irascible and the law does not follow him. Under letter pe it writes that Aharon, Eli, Ezra and Hillel are from one spark. “Which Moses performed before the eyes of all Israel”: the final letters spell Hillel.

E) Herod greatly honored Hillel, because he favored his reign (see above, Shammai); in his youth he prophesied concerning his kingship. He was called Hillel the Babylonian, being among Babylonia’s well-born, as stated in chapter Asarah Yuchasin. He went up to the Land of Israel and spoke Babylonia’s language. He stated four things in the Mishnah: “One who spreads a name loses his name”; likewise, “Turn it over …”; “Because you drowned others, they drowned you ….” He also said, “An ignorant person is not sin-fearing” (see Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the Elder). He studied Torah in poverty and holds the poor accountable: chapter Amar Lahem HaMemunneh, 35b. Of him it is said: whoever fulfills Torah in poverty will ultimately fulfill it in wealth. In Sotah, chapter Hayah Notel, 21, end of side a: Hillel and Shevna were brothers; Hillel engaged in Torah, Shevna in business. At the end he said, “Come, let us combine and divide.” A heavenly voice declared, “If a man gives all the wealth of his house …,” because he had not given him support before he began studying, as with Shimon, Azaryah’s brother (see his entry). Hillel was of the aspect of the last he of the divine name; the numerical value is Adonai, the secret of poverty, poor and needy, having nothing of its own (see Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom). From Moses until the sons of Beteira they recited 600 orders of Mishnah. Hillel arranged six orders orally and increased Torah in Israel. Soferim chapter 16: Hillel left no wisdom unlearned, even all the languages and speech of palms (see Arukh), mountains, hills, trees, wild and domestic animals, demons, and the parables of launderers and foxes. At the end of Sheviit, and in Tosafot, Gittin 36, end of side a: he instituted the prozbul because he knew prophetically that the Temple would be destroyed; thus Rabbenu Tam explains. A heavenly voice declared him worthy of the Divine Presence resting upon him: Sotah 48b; Sanhedrin 11a; Shir HaShirim Rabbah, on “If she is a wall.” He is called Ezra’s student. At the end of Sukkah chapter 1, Resh Lakish said: when Torah was forgotten from Israel, Ezra came up and established it; it was forgotten again, and Hillel the Babylonian came up and established it. He had eighty students: the greatest was Yonatan ben Uzziel and the least Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai, Sukkah chapter 2, 28a; Bava Batra, Yesh Nochalin, 134a. Onkelos, who translated the Torah, was in his days. Ben Hi Hi and Ben Bag Bag said to him. The elders of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel went to visit Rabbi Yochanan HaChoranit; they went to Rabbi Yochanan ben Beteira (see his entry). His burial is in Kefar Meron (see Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai).
